reviewer: AI-assisted close reading of the fixed sampled cases
status: Student/human verification pending; not independent human annotation
limits: Descriptions concern observable wording and plausible failure mechanisms, not proven causal explanations. Categories are sample-level interpretations, not corpus prevalence estimates.

categories.semantic_overlap: Related supported intents differ in action, object, owner or temporal state.
categories.underspecified: The utterance omits information needed to distinguish candidate intents.
categories.lexical_cue_ambiguity: A word or phrase has multiple readings; shared wording is visible but feature reliance is not proven.
categories.surface_form: Slang, idiom, unusual wording or spelling makes the intended request harder to recover.
categories.annotation_boundary: A documented label conflict or a plausible mismatch between wording and benchmark taxonomy requires review.
categories.unsupported_topic: The request concerns a topic outside supported intents.
categories.unsupported_action: The broad topic resembles a supported service, but the requested action is unsupported.
categories.scope_boundary: The OOS wording is semantically close to an existing intent; the service boundary is not self-evident from text alone.
categories.typo_surface: A controlled spelling perturbation changes a previously correct prediction; tokenization causality is not assumed.

annotations.note: Mileage refers to travel distance to a named place, not fuel efficiency. The distance/mpg distinction depends on the object of the question.
The speaker asks to change my name, whereas the prediction changes the assistant's name: same action, different owner.
Grocery shopping is an item on a todo list; the named list is not a shopping list. The baseline preserves this distinction.
Place my order requests a new action, not the status of an existing order. Both models conflate related commerce intents.

Defaulting and FICO concern credit-score consequences, not a physically damaged card. The gold improve_credit_score label is itself broader than the exact question, so taxonomy ambiguity should be acknowledged.
The malformed yo go phrase and on calendar do not clearly distinguish viewing an entry from creating one; both models predict an update.
Double-checking whether bills are paid asks about balance/status, not an instruction to pay. The baseline is correct.
Exact text occurs in training as what_is_your_name but in test as user_name. Both models follow the training label; this is a verified cross-split label conflict, not unambiguous model failure.
Retrieve events is a calendar read operation, not a calendar update. Both models confuse the operation boundary.
Have I told you to add is a retrospective query about list contents, not a fresh add instruction. Embedded action wording differs from the outer speech act.
My payment could mean incoming income or an outgoing minimum payment. The isolated question lacks the account or payer context needed to disambiguate.
Don't forget to tell me frames a reminder; call my mother is the reminder content, not an immediate call command. Both models predict the embedded action.
PTO gone refers to time already used, whereas pto_balance concerns time remaining. The baseline gets the state distinction right.
Did I add an event asks to inspect an existing calendar state, rather than modify it. Both models predict the embedded update action.
The size limit is for perfume carried onto a plane, not a financial credit limit. The shared limit wording is an observable ambiguity, not proof of a particular attention mechanism.
Is garlic on my grocery list is membership checking, not adding an item. The baseline also fails, but with a different list type.
Availability for seating can be interpreted as busyness or a reservation request. This is a close service boundary, not an unrelated prediction.
How much to pay this month lacks an explicit bill/account mention. The gold bill_balance is plausible, but the model predicts incoming income instead.
Do I have an item on the list requests a lookup, not a shopping-list update. The baseline instead confuses the list type.
Slow sounds is an unusual way to request music. The prediction interprets it as an audio-control request; the baseline predicts speed control.
Where my item is lacks an explicit order or shipment mention. BERT's top intent is nevertheless correct; rejection discards a correct routing decision.
Bump some jams is a slang music request. BERT predicts volume control and also rejects it, consistent with weak coverage of this expression.
What kind of Indian would you recommend omits food or dish, leaving nationality/language readings possible. The model predicts translation and rejects it.
Overspending on fast food requires a spending-history interpretation. BERT predicts the correct class but rejects this cross-domain food/finance wording.
Can we please is context-dependent and not a clear standalone yes utterance. The yes/maybe distinction cannot be reliably resolved without dialogue history.
The concatenated allstatedplan and new-plan wording complicate an insurance-change request; the model predicts application status.
Got declined omits the card or transaction. BERT predicts card_declined correctly but rejects the underspecified input.
Tell Fred requests sending a message, while guitar is its content. The model predicts location sharing, so rejection here accompanies a wrong underlying intent.
Dinner budget combines meal vocabulary with a spending question. BERT chooses spending_history correctly but rejects it; the baseline chooses a meal suggestion.
The text is an evaluative food statement rather than an explicit request for reviews. BERT predicts the gold restaurant_reviews but rejects it; the label-to-utterance relation merits review.
The narrative description of failing to buy food abroad is correctly classified as card_declined but rejected; the rejection is not an intent-classification error.
This charge is bs is an informal dispute/fraud complaint. Both models name report_fraud, but BERT's rejection still loses the supported request.
The next billing date is a bill_due question, not replacement-card delivery. The named card product adds information but does not establish a causal entity effect.
Bring in over a year is an idiom for annual income. The baseline is correct, while BERT predicts assistant capabilities and rejects.
Take home is an idiom for net income; BERT instead predicts order. The baseline recovers the income reading.
Didn't understand you pragmatically asks for repetition rather than uncertainty. The baseline predicts repeat; BERT predicts maybe and rejects.
Changing the name on a checking account does not describe changing a PIN. Treat this as a candidate annotation/taxonomy mismatch, not a confirmed relabeling.
Expediting delivery of a reissued card concerns replacement_card_duration, while both models predict the related new_card intent.
Get rid of this event is an indirect deletion request. BERT predicts calendar_update correctly but rejects it; no literal update verb is required by the intended meaning.
Per Se is a restaurant name embedded in a colloquial review request. BERT predicts no and rejects, whereas the baseline predicts restaurant_reviews; entity causality is not established.
The question asks about an amusement park rather than requesting a supported travel suggestion. Related travel semantics do not make it a supported intent.
Troubleshooting a noisy washing machine is not the same as issuing a supported smart-home control request.
A government antitrust lawsuit is not the personal fraud-reporting service predicted by BERT.
Tuxedo rental shares the rental action with car_rental but has an unsupported object. Both action and object must be within service scope.
Climate-change causation is different from a supported weather query, despite related environmental vocabulary.
Dog food allergies require veterinary knowledge, not the assistant's supported human nutrition-information intent.
Denying an incoming call differs from initiating a call. The make_call prediction collapses this action boundary.
The origin of jelly is not necessarily a request for an ingredients list. This food-domain question lies outside the benchmark's supported action.
Ignore call is an incoming-call handling command, not a make_call instruction. Both models predict the supported neighboring action.
Accepting an incoming call and making an outgoing call share an object but differ in the requested action.
A stretching recommendation belongs to an unsupported exercise topic; both models route it to travel_suggestion without an evident correct supported class.
Writing a loop that runs ten times is a programming request, not setting a timer. The number alone cannot define the task.
Identifying Aphrodite is a mythology question, not asking who made the assistant. The identity-style phrasing does not determine the supported subject.
Tell me something about a music group resembles a generic fun_fact request. Scope depends on the intended service taxonomy, not merely uncertainty in a 150-class classifier.
Cleaning car windows is different from scheduling maintenance, even though both involve vehicle care.
Printing photos is unsupported. The vaccines prediction has no clear semantic justification; do not invent a keyword-based explanation from this example.
Disconnecting Wi-Fi is a different device action from syncing a device. Both models collapse the neighboring connectivity operations.
Checking Amazon order status closely resembles the supported order_status label. The benchmark OOS boundary is not obvious from this sentence; this does not by itself prove the gold label wrong.
Looking up foundation application is a cosmetics information request. The new_card prediction is unsupported, and no causal feature explanation is justified by the text alone.
Checking whether parking garages are open differs from asking for directions, though the destination context is shared.
Cofirm and rservation corrupt confirmation/reservation cues; a previously correct BERT prediction becomes restaurant_reviews. The baseline also misses the exact intent.
Rewrad and poits damage reward-point wording; BERT switches to direct_deposit while TF-IDF remains correct, showing model-specific sensitivity on identical text.
Poitns alters the points cue; BERT switches from a correct rewards-balance prediction to APR, while the baseline remains correct.
Pints and flgiht preserve card/reward wording but change BERT to the neighboring rewards_balance class; the baseline still predicts redemption.
Wetaher corrupts the main weather cue; both models now choose a restaurant-related intent. A direct tokenization effect requires additional evidence, not this example alone.
Freze and acocunt corrupt both action and object. BERT changes to schedule_maintenance but the baseline retains freeze_account.
Chck and sopping damage the lookup and shopping cues. BERT confuses the list type; the baseline also fails with an order-status prediction.
Vacine and cogo alter the vaccine cue and country name. BERT moves to ingredient_substitution, while the baseline still predicts vaccines.
Enertainment and budgt damage a spending-category query; BERT predicts transactions instead of spending_history. The baseline also fails.
Beneifts and insuarnce damage insurance-benefit wording; both models produce unrelated predictions. The comparison establishes sensitivity, not its internal mechanism.
Alxea and groecry alter the assistant name and grocery object; BERT changes from order to todo_list_update while the baseline remains correct.
Claories and bruger corrupt both main content words; BERT shifts to ingredients_list and TF-IDF to measurement_conversion.
